intent: Show that people in transit-oriented developments drive less and use public transit, biking, and walking more than the national average.

requirements.question: How do trip shares differ between transit-oriented developments and the national average?

units.claim: The car share is lower in transit-oriented developments: 45% vs 90% nationally (45 percentage points lower).
accept: transit-oriented developments have a lower car share
45 percentage points lower for car trips
reject: saying car use is higher there
units.evidence: Two bars for car use: 45% at transit-oriented developments vs 90% nationally.

units.claim: Public transit, biking, and walking shares are higher in transit-oriented developments: 30% vs 6%, 3% vs 1%, and 22% vs 3%.
accept: all three non-car modes are higher
reject: missing any of the three modes
saying one of the three is lower
units.evidence: Bar pairs for public transit, biking and walking all show the development value higher.
